entries.name: $RESET
entries.purpose: power-on and RESET entry: disable interrupts, clear A, and jump to the cold-start code at 0674H
entries.note: RST 00H continues at 0674H here; on the Model III it continues at 3015H (decker 51)

entries.name: SYNCHK
entries.purpose: check that (HL) equals the byte after the RST, else syntax error; then get the next text character

entries.name: GETPC
entries.purpose: POP HL then JP (HL): return with the caller's return address in HL, so relocatable code can find itself

entries.name: DISKBOOT
entries.purpose: warm restart: jump to the disk bootstrap loader at 069FH without re-initializing the system

entries.name: NEXTCHAR
entries.purpose: step HL to the next non-blank text character; carry for a digit, zero at a colon or end of line

entries.name: GETDEV
entries.purpose: read a byte into A from the device whose control block DE addresses; Z if it was ready

entries.name: CMPHLDE
entries.purpose: compare HL with DE as unsigned 16-bit numbers; Z if equal, carry if DE is the larger

entries.name: PUTDEV
entries.purpose: send the byte in A to the device whose control block DE points to; Z is set if the device was ready

entries.name: TESTNTF
entries.purpose: test the number type flag at 40AFH; the flags show the type and A returns the type minus 3

entries.name: BREAKRST
entries.purpose: jump through the vector at 400CH, a no-op without a disk system and a DOS hook for BREAK and overlays

entries.name: $KBCHAR
entries.purpose: scan the keyboard once: A returns the key's character code, or zero if no key is down (DE is used)

entries.name: DEBUGRST
entries.purpose: jump through the vector at 400FH, which a disk system uses as its DEBUG entry

entries.name: $VDCHAR
entries.purpose: display the character in A at the cursor, carrying out control codes (DE is used)

entries.name: INTRST
entries.purpose: jump through the vector at 4012H, which is EI and RET without a disk system

entries.name: $PRCHAR
entries.purpose: send A to the line printer when it is ready; with A zero it only returns the printer status in Z

entries.name: $KBLINE
entries.purpose: read a line from the keyboard by jumping to the line-input routine at 05D9H

entries.name: $KBWAIT
entries.purpose: wait until a key is pressed and return its character in A, by calling 002BH in a loop (DE is used)

entries.name: CTRLCHARTAB
entries.purpose: table of the control codes for ENTER, CLEAR, BREAK, the arrow keys, and space: eight two-byte entries
entries.note: on the Model III this address is $RSRCV, the RS-232-C receive routine (decker 19)

entries.name: $DELAY
entries.purpose: pause set by BC: about 14.66 microseconds a count, and about a second at BC of zero
entries.note: each count takes about 14.66 microseconds here and about 14.80 on the Model III, whose loop has an extra instruction (decker 53)

entries.name: NMIENTRY
entries.purpose: RESET button entry: restart through 0000H if a disk controller is present, else go to BASIC Ready at 06CCH
entries.note: the Model III handler tests port E4H for a disk interrupt instead (decker 54)

entries.name: ERR_L3
entries.purpose: raise the L3 ERROR, where the Disk BASIC command vectors from 4152H point when no Disk BASIC is loaded

entries.name: BASICPOINT
entries.purpose: BASIC POINT entry point; the SET and RESET entries follow at 0135H and 0138H

entries.name: BASICSET
entries.purpose: BASIC SET entry point

entries.name: BASICRESET
entries.purpose: BASIC RESET entry point

entries.name: PIXELOP
entries.purpose: pixel routine behind SET, RESET, and POINT: function and X on the stack, Y in A, then JP here

entries.name: $VDCLS
entries.purpose: clear the screen and home the cursor, as BASIC CLS does

entries.name: BASICRANDOM
entries.purpose: the core of BASIC RANDOM: store the Z80 refresh register in the seed byte at 40ABH and return

entries.name: CASBITOUT
entries.purpose: write one bit to the cassette as pulses with delay loops between them (uses AF, B, and HL)
entries.note: on the Model III this address is $PRSCN, the print-screen routine (decker 16, 80)

entries.name: $CSOFF
entries.purpose: turn the cassette motor off

entries.name: CASDEFDRIVE
entries.purpose: choose the cassette drive from BASIC text (# then -1 or -2 and a comma, else drive 1), then select it

entries.name: CASDRVSEL
entries.purpose: select the cassette drive named by A (0 first, 1 second) and turn its motor on
entries.note: the Model III keeps this address only as XOR A; RET, so Model I software that calls it still runs (decker 17)

entries.name: CASMOTORON
entries.purpose: turn the cassette motor on without selecting a drive, so the drive chosen earlier stays selected

entries.name: CASINRESET
entries.purpose: reset the cassette input at port FFH (uses AF and HL)

entries.name: CASBLINK
entries.purpose: blink the right-hand asterisk at the top right of the screen while a tape loads (uses AF)
entries.note: on the Model III this address only jumps to 0212H, which clears A and returns (decker 17)

entries.name: $CSIN
entries.purpose: read one byte from the cassette into A, with BC, DE, and HL kept

entries.name: CASBITIN
entries.purpose: read one bit from the cassette and shift it into A; 0235H calls it eight times for a byte (uses AF and HL)

entries.name: $CSOUT
entries.purpose: write the byte in A to the cassette, with BC, DE, and HL kept

entries.name: CSHWRSEL
entries.purpose: select the cassette drive through 01FEH and turn the motor on, then write the leader and sync byte at 0287H
entries.note: on the Model III this address holds only JP 0287H (decker 17)

entries.name: $CSHWR
entries.purpose: write the cassette leader and the A5H sync byte; the motor must already be on, which 0284H arranges
entries.note: unlike the Model III routine at this address, this one does not turn the cassette on (decker 17)

entries.name: CSHINSEL
entries.purpose: select the cassette drive through 01FEH and turn the motor on, then look for the leader and sync byte at 0296H
entries.note: on the Model III this address holds only JP 0243H (decker 17)

entries.name: $CSHIN
entries.purpose: read the cassette past the leader and the A5H sync byte, then show two asterisks; the motor must be on
entries.note: unlike the Model III routine at this address, this one does not turn the cassette on (decker 17)

entries.name: BASICSYSTEM
entries.purpose: main routine of the BASIC SYSTEM command, which loads a machine-language tape
entries.note: BASIC enters the command at 02B2H (decker 121), which calls the DOS link at 41E2H (decker 74) and falls into this address; the Model III code differs inside it, at 02E2H-02E4H, where INC HL and JR NZ,02D1H come in the opposite order (decker 82)

entries.name: CSINWORD
entries.purpose: read two bytes from a running cassette into HL, low byte first, as a SYSTEM tape's entry address is read

entries.name: OUTCHAR
entries.purpose: send A to the output device that the flag at 409CH selects: video, printer, or cassette

entries.name: VDCHARCOL
entries.purpose: display A as 0033H does but keep DE, and refresh the cursor column that TAB reads at 40A6H

entries.name: CURCOLUMN
entries.purpose: return the cursor column on its line in A: 0 to 63, or 0 to 31 in 32-character mode

entries.name: KBSAVEDE
entries.purpose: scan the keyboard like 002BH but keep DE; it first calls the DOS link at 41C4H, which an entry at 035BH skips
entries.note: Paay (p. 7) lists the same routine at 035BH, just past the DOS link

entries.name: KBINBUF
entries.purpose: read a line from the keyboard into the BASIC input buffer with echo, 240 characters at most; carry if BREAK

entries.name: KBWAITDE
entries.purpose: wait for a key like 0049H but keep DE, by calling 0358H in a loop

entries.name: DEVRESETPRT
entries.purpose: select video as the output device again, first ending a partly printed printer line with a carriage return

entries.name: PRTCR
entries.purpose: send a carriage return to the printer through 039CH

entries.name: PRTCHARPOS
entries.purpose: send A to the printer, keeping all registers; counts the line position at 409BH, turns a line feed into CR

entries.name: IODISPATCH
entries.purpose: the I/O driver entry routine behind 0013H and 001BH: runs the driver the control block at DE names
entries.note: the Model III has its printer driver, PRDRIVER, at this address; its I/O driver entry routine is at 0674H (decker 82)

entries.name: KBDRIVER
entries.purpose: the Model I keyboard driver that the keyboard control block points to: scans the keys, returns ASCII in A
entries.note: the Model III keeps its keyboard driver at 3024H (decker 14)

entries.name: VDDRIVER
entries.purpose: the Model I video driver that the video control block points to: shows the character in C, scrolls
entries.note: the Model III keeps its video driver at 0473H (decker 15)

entries.name: VD64MODE
entries.purpose: switch the display to 64-character mode (uses A)

entries.name: VD32MODE
entries.purpose: switch the display to 32-character mode (uses A and HL)

entries.name: VDCLRTOEND
entries.purpose: clear the screen from the address in HL to the end of video memory (uses DE and A)

entries.name: PRDRIVER
entries.purpose: the Model I printer driver, whose address the printer control block holds: it prints the character in C
entries.note: the Model III keeps its printer driver at 03C2H (decker 16)

entries.name: PRTTEST
entries.purpose: read the printer status at 37E8H; Z is set when the printer is ready to take a character (uses AF)
entries.note: the Model III keeps this routine at 044BH (decker 16)

entries.name: LINEINPUT
entries.purpose: echoing line input into the buffer at HL, B characters at most, ended by ENTER or BREAK; B returns the length

entries.name: READYREENTRY
entries.purpose: return to BASIC Ready without the false Out of Memory message, by loading BC with 1A18H and jumping to 19AEH
entries.note: on the Model III 06CCH is part of the LIST command and no longer returns to BASIC (decker 54, 82)

entries.name: ERR_OV
entries.purpose: raise the OV ERROR (overflow)

entries.name: MUL10SNG
entries.purpose: multiply the single-precision accumulator by 10

entries.name: CINT
entries.purpose: convert the accumulator to an integer in HL; a USR routine calls this to take its argument

entries.name: HLTOACC
entries.purpose: make the integer in HL the accumulator's value; a USR routine jumps here to hand its result back to BASIC

entries.name: CHKSTRING
entries.purpose: return if the accumulator holds a string, else raise a type mismatch error (BC, DE, and HL kept)

entries.name: ERR_TM
entries.purpose: raise the TM ERROR (type mismatch)

entries.name: ASCTONUM
entries.purpose: read the numeric text at HL into the accumulator, in the smallest number type that holds it

entries.name: OUTHLDEC
entries.purpose: print the positive integer in HL in decimal on the device that 409CH selects

entries.name: ERR_SN
entries.purpose: raise the SN ERROR (syntax error)

entries.name: BASICERROR
entries.purpose: BASIC error exit: put the even error code, 0 to 2CH, in E and jump here

entries.name: READYALT
entries.purpose: return to BASIC Ready without a false Out of Memory message: load BC with 1A18H, then jump here

entries.name: $READY
entries.purpose: return to BASIC Ready by jumping here, the entry Radio Shack documents; may leave a false Out of Memory error

entries.name: FIXLINEPTRS
entries.purpose: recompute the forward line pointers of the BASIC program, as a renumbering program needs (uses A, HL, DE)

entries.name: FINDLINE
entries.purpose: find the BASIC line numbered DE: carry if found, BC at that line and HL at the next one (uses AF, BC, and HL)

entries.name: INPROMPT
entries.purpose: show a question mark and a space, then read a line as 0361H does

entries.name: ERR_FC
entries.purpose: raise the FC ERROR (illegal function call)

entries.name: ASCTODE
entries.purpose: read the unsigned decimal number at HL into DE; HL returns at the delimiter

entries.name: NEWLINE
entries.purpose: send a carriage return to the output device unless the cursor is already at the start of a line

entries.name: OUTCR
entries.purpose: send a carriage return to the device that 409CH selects

entries.name: TABTO
entries.purpose: BASIC TAB on the device 409CH selects: E is the column, HL the text to print or a zero byte

entries.name: DEVRESETCAS
entries.purpose: select video as the output device again, first switching the cassette off if it was in use

entries.name: INPUTSTMT
entries.purpose: BASIC INPUT: show the prompt at HL if any, read the line, and assign the variables that follow

entries.name: EVALEXPR
entries.purpose: evaluate the BASIC expression at HL into the accumulator; it ends at a zero, comma, ) or colon, where HL returns

entries.name: FINDVAR
entries.purpose: find or create the BASIC variable named at HL; DE returns its address (a string's three-byte vector)

entries.name: OUTSTR
entries.purpose: print the string at HL, ended by a zero byte or a quote, on the device 409CH selects, as PRINT does

entries.name: ACCTODE
entries.purpose: convert the accumulator to an integer in DE; Z is set if the result is 255 or less

entries.name: OUTSTRZ
entries.purpose: print the zero-terminated string at HL on the device that 409CH selects, through 032AH

entries.name: BASICCSAVE
entries.purpose: BASIC CSAVE: save the program to cassette, with HL at the quoted one-character file name

entries.name: BASICCLOAD
entries.purpose: BASIC CLOAD: load or verify a program from cassette; it ends at BASIC Ready instead of returning

entries.name: SYNCHKVEC
entries.purpose: jump vector for RST 08H, set at start-up to continue at 1C96H, the syntax-check code

entries.name: NEXTCHARVEC
entries.purpose: jump vector for RST 10H, set at start-up to continue at 1D78H, the next-character code

entries.name: CMPHLDEVEC
entries.purpose: jump vector for RST 18H, set at start-up to continue at 1C90H, the HL and DE compare

entries.name: TESTNTFVEC
entries.purpose: jump vector for RST 20H, set at start-up to continue at 25D9H, the number-type test

entries.name: BREAKVEC
entries.purpose: RST 28H's RAM jump vector: a lone RET without a disk system; the keyboard driver calls it on BREAK

entries.name: DEBUGVEC
entries.purpose: jump vector for RST 30H, a lone RET without a disk system; a DOS uses it as its DEBUG entry

entries.name: INTVEC
entries.purpose: RST 38H's RAM jump vector: EI and RET without a disk system, a disk system's interrupt entry with one

entries.name: KBDCB
entries.purpose: start of the 8-byte keyboard control block, its device type byte, normally 1 (read only)
entries.note: LDOS 5.1 names the whole 8-byte keyboard control block KIDCB$ (4015H-401CH, ldos51 6-29); this table keeps the ROM's own field names

entries.name: KBDRVADDR
entries.purpose: address of the keyboard driver, which the keyboard scan jumps to on each scan

entries.name: VDDCB
entries.purpose: start of the 8-byte video control block, its device type byte, normally 7 (read and write)
entries.note: LDOS 5.1 names the whole 8-byte video control block DODCB$ (401DH-4024H, ldos51 6-29); this table keeps the ROM's own field names

entries.name: VDDRVADDR
entries.purpose: address of the video driver, which the video control block points to

entries.name: CURADDR
entries.purpose: address of the cursor in video memory, low byte first, in the range 3C00H to 3FFFH

entries.name: PRDCB
entries.purpose: start of the 8-byte printer control block, its device type byte, normally 6 (write only)
entries.note: LDOS 5.1 names the whole 8-byte printer control block PRDCB$ (4025H-402CH, ldos51 6-29); this table keeps the ROM's own field names

entries.name: PRDRVADDR
entries.purpose: address of the printer driver; pointing it at the video driver sends LPRINT to the screen, and the reverse

entries.name: PRTPAGELEN
entries.purpose: lines per page for the printer, 67 at start-up
entries.note: start-up sets 67 on both machines; the Model III counts the page length plus one, so a 66-line form wants 66 here (decker 9)

entries.name: PRTLINECNT
entries.purpose: lines already printed on the current page
entries.note: the Model III holds this count plus one (decker 9)

entries.name: KBROWS
entries.purpose: last state of the seven keyboard rows (3801H-3840H), so a scan can tell a new press from a held key

entries.name: PORTFFBITS
entries.purpose: bits last written to port FFH: bit 3 is 32-character video, bit 2 the cassette relay, bits 1-0 the audio
entries.note: Paay calls this the print size flag, 0 for 64 characters and F8H for 32; Decker gives it as the bits last sent to port FFH (decker 11); the Model III keeps its port ECH bits at 4210H (decker 12)

entries.name: USRVEC
entries.purpose: address of the USR routine, low byte first; BASIC programs POKE it into 16526 and 16527

entries.name: INPORT
entries.purpose: RAM routine IN A,(n) then RET: poke the port number n into its second byte at 4094H before calling it

entries.name: OUTPORT
entries.purpose: RAM routine OUT (n),A then RET: poke the port number n into its second byte at 4097H before calling it

entries.name: INKEYBUF
entries.purpose: key buffer for INKEY$: a non-zero value here is returned before the keyboard is scanned

entries.name: PRTCOLUMN
entries.purpose: number of characters already sent to the printer on the current line, for a TAB that works past column 63

entries.name: OUTDEVFLAG
entries.purpose: output device for the general output routines: 0 video, 1 printer, 255 cassette

entries.name: PROGSTART
entries.purpose: pointer to the start of the BASIC program text; the byte just below it must be zero

entries.name: LINEPOS
entries.purpose: cursor column on the current video line, which TAB and POS read

entries.name: IOBUFPTR
entries.purpose: pointer to the BASIC input buffer, used by the line-input routines and while BASIC tokenizes a line

entries.name: NTF
entries.purpose: number type flag for the accumulator: 2 integer, 3 string, 4 single precision, 8 double precision

entries.name: MEMTOP
entries.purpose: pointer to the last memory address BASIC may use, set from the answer to MEMORY SIZE?

entries.name: VARSTART
entries.purpose: pointer to the simple variables, which is also the end of the BASIC program

entries.name: ARRAYSTART
entries.purpose: pointer to the start of the array variables

entries.name: FREESTART
entries.purpose: pointer to the end of the arrays, where free memory begins

entries.name: ACC
entries.purpose: the arithmetic accumulator: an integer fills 4121H-4122H, a single 4121H-4124H, and a double all eight bytes

entries.name: AACC
entries.purpose: the auxiliary accumulator that the double-precision routines use, 4127H to 412EH
